title: Full of facts, but empty of change: integrate ideas instead of collecting them
summary: Cris Pop argues that learning is not progress unless ideas get integrated into daily life. He re-reads sources until they stop yielding, tests one idea for a week, cuts inputs that don't serve a current problem, teaches only what he has lived, and listens diagnostically to find what people actually need.

principles.text: An insight is worthless until it lives in a system you use every day.
principles.quote: If it doesn’t live in your day-to-day life, it doesn’t live at all.

principles.text: Squeeze one resource dry (re-read, rewatch) before moving to the next.
principles.quote: I usually read the same book a few times.

principles.text: Test one idea at a time by building something around it for a week.
principles.quote: One idea. One week. Build something around it.

principles.text: Cut inputs that don't solve a problem you face right now, even good ones.
principles.quote: Ask yourself, is this solving a problem I’m facing right now?

principles.text: Only teach what you've tested and failed with yourself.
principles.quote: Teach from the scars, not the scripts.

principles.text: Listen diagnostically to find where the real need and confusion live before offering insight.
principles.quote: You can’t teach with precision if you haven’t first listened with obsession.
